intake-triage.goal: Turn the reported fault into one reproducible test and the correct repair route.
intake-triage.startHere: Ask the user to show the failing task once. Record the exact error, last working time, affected users and whether important data has another copy.

tools.why: Identify the process involved in the failure.
Check drive warnings before repair writes.
Identifying the actual USB port, hub, device and negotiated connection when a printer, scanner or peripheral disconnects or runs slowly.
Collecting battery and sleep evidence before changing hardware or power policy.

resources.label: Intake and handoff sheet
resources.description: Capture the symptom, permission, recovery plan and acceptance test.

resources.label: Reliability history command
resources.description: Open failure history with perfmon /rel.

resources.label: Windows recovery choices
resources.description: Check which recovery action preserves files and applications.

decisions.symptom: The error appears in one app or account
decisions.action: Repeat the same task in another approved account or app; record what changes.
decisions.expected: The fault is scoped to an app, profile or wider device problem.

decisions.symptom: Several users or devices fail together
decisions.action: Compare one known-working device and the same service; use the office-outage route when the dependency is shared.
decisions.expected: The ticket identifies the shared service and its recovery owner.

decisions.symptom: The timing or cause is unclear
decisions.action: Press Win+R, run perfmon /rel, select the failure time and open technical details.
decisions.expected: A dated failure or recent change can be compared with the user’s timeline.

decisions.symptom: A drive clicks, disappears or reports repeated I/O errors
decisions.action: Stop ordinary repair and route to failing-drive recovery before scans or file-system repairs.
decisions.expected: The source is preserved and the imaging or specialist decision is recorded.

doneWhen: One exact reproduction and expected outcome are recorded.
The next guide, responsible technician and recoverable data copy are identified.
escalateWhen: Active encryption or spreading compromise requires the incident route.
The next action would risk the only usable data copy.

malware-removal.goal: Remove the identified threat, close its entry point and prove the endpoint is usable after restart.
malware-removal.startHere: If encryption, privileged-account compromise or multiple affected devices are present, isolate and use the incident route. Otherwise record detections and keep one real-time protection product.

tools.why: Fresh on-demand scan and a readable result log.
Focused adware and browser-hijacker cleanup.
Inspect evidence-backed startup persistence.
Offline scan when the documented platform and recovery requirements are met.
Use existing endpoint telemetry for investigation; plan new deployment after active evidence-preservation needs are resolved.

resources.label: Safety Scanner results and expiry
resources.description: Read the completion result and %SYSTEMROOT%\debug\msert.log.

resources.label: AdwCleaner scan and review
resources.description: Review detected items before cleanup and retain the report.

resources.label: Contain ransomware or a wider compromise
resources.description: Use the incident route for active encryption, lateral spread or privileged-account compromise.

resources.label: Defender Offline requirements
resources.description: Check platform, primary antivirus, WinRE and BitLocker preparation.

resources.label: Trusted reinstall procedure
resources.description: Preserve required evidence and data before a clean installation.

decisions.symptom: The installed protection reports a threat
decisions.action: Update through an approved channel, run its full scan and quarantine identified detections; retain the report.
decisions.expected: The run has a completion state and a recorded action for every detection.

decisions.symptom: Adware, unwanted extensions or browser redirection dominate
decisions.action: Run AdwCleaner, review its proposed changes and restore the intended browser extensions, search and notification settings.
decisions.expected: The original browser task works and unwanted behavior does not return after restart.

decisions.symptom: A second on-demand check is needed
decisions.action: Download a fresh Microsoft Safety Scanner from a clean PC, run a Full scan and read the detailed log.
decisions.expected: Completed coverage, detections and unresolved items are recorded; a cancelled run is not marked clean.

decisions.symptom: The same detection returns after reboot
decisions.action: Inspect the relevant Autoruns entry and documented offline-scan prerequisites; use the rebuild decision if integrity remains uncertain.
decisions.expected: The persistence cause is explained or a clean recovery plan replaces repeated scanner loops.

doneWhen: Protection is healthy after reboot and there are no unresolved detections.
The original task and browser behavior remain correct.
Compromised accounts and sessions have a separate documented resolution.
escalateWhen: Ransomware, lateral spread or privileged access is suspected.
Detections recur or scan coverage and system integrity cannot be established.

ransomware-response.goal: Contain spread, preserve useful evidence and recover through a controlled clean environment.
ransomware-response.startHere: Disconnect affected network access and contact the incident lead through a clean channel. Do not attach backups to the affected environment.

tools.why: Use existing endpoint telemetry for investigation; plan new deployment after active evidence-preservation needs are resolved.

resources.label: CISA ransomware response checklist
resources.description: Isolation, evidence preservation and recovery priorities.

resources.label: Microsoft incident-response approach
resources.description: Scope compromised systems, identities and recovery dependencies.

resources.label: Recovery acceptance evidence
resources.description: Record clean media, restored data and return-to-service proof.

decisions.symptom: Files are being encrypted or several endpoints are affected
decisions.action: Isolate network links or the affected switch segment with the incident lead; keep isolated devices powered when feasible for evidence.
decisions.expected: Spread is contained and the action time and affected scope are recorded.

decisions.symptom: Isolation is impossible and damage continues
decisions.action: Have the incident lead decide whether shutdown is necessary, recording the loss of volatile evidence.
decisions.expected: Continuing harm is stopped with an explicit evidence tradeoff.

decisions.symptom: Backups appear reachable from compromised systems
decisions.action: Separate their access path and inspect recovery copies from a known-clean administration device.
decisions.expected: At least one usable recovery copy is protected from the incident.

decisions.symptom: A team is ready to restore services
decisions.action: Agree dependency order, rebuild affected systems from trusted media and test restored business tasks before reconnection.
decisions.expected: The incident lead has evidence for release, including account/session containment.

doneWhen: Affected systems and identities have a documented scope and owner.
Clean restoration passes the actual business workflow.
The incident lead authorizes reconnection and records remaining unknowns.
escalateWhen: An action would overwrite evidence or the only recovery copy.
Identity compromise or infrastructure recovery exceeds the responder’s authority or capability.

slow-pc.goal: Find the resource or dependency causing the delay and measure the same task after the repair.
slow-pc.startHere: Time one slow action. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc and watch CPU, memory and disk while reproducing it; check drive health before a heavy scan.

tools.why: Identify the busy process and its owner.
Capture a short, filtered file or registry stall.
Explain capacity use on healthy storage.
Separate storage warnings from ordinary software lag.
Optional quick storage performance baseline on healthy media only; choose the intended drive and record comparable settings.
Collecting battery and sleep evidence before changing hardware or power policy.
Measure a reproducible storage-performance problem on healthy media with a bounded test file.

resources.label: Process Explorer usage
resources.description: Inspect the exact process before stopping or changing it.

resources.label: Process Monitor filtering
resources.description: Limit capture to the affected process and interval.

resources.label: Windows performance tracing
resources.description: Use a measured trace when ordinary process views do not explain the delay.

decisions.symptom: CPU stays high during the slow task
decisions.action: Sort by CPU in Task Manager; inspect the identified process in Process Explorer and check its image path and owner.
decisions.expected: One process or service correlates with the delay.

decisions.symptom: Memory pressure rises as responsiveness falls
decisions.action: Check Task Manager > Performance > Memory, then close an agreed nonessential workload and repeat the task.
decisions.expected: The before/after result distinguishes workload pressure from another cause.

decisions.symptom: Disk activity stalls the system
decisions.action: Check health first; on stable media use a short Process Monitor capture filtered to the affected process and path.
decisions.expected: The slow I/O path is identified, or failing storage is routed to recovery.

decisions.symptom: The healthy system drive is nearly full
decisions.action: Use WinDirStat to identify the largest owned folders; remove only approved content through supported cleanup controls.
decisions.expected: Free space improves and the original application still works.

decisions.symptom: Only a task using a share or online service is slow
decisions.action: Compare an approved local equivalent and follow the network guide for the remote dependency.
decisions.expected: The evidence separates local performance from service or network latency.

decisions.symptom: Storage is healthy but unusually slow, or a replacement drive needs a baseline
decisions.action: Check CrystalDiskInfo first. If storage is stable and backed up, use CrystalDiskMark with a bounded test file on the intended drive; compare the same profile, test size, count, connection and software version. Stop on disconnects or I/O errors.
decisions.expected: A reproducible read/write baseline for that drive, separate from SMART health; abnormal results lead to cable, port, controller or workload investigation, not a health diagnosis.

doneWhen: The same workload has a recorded before/after result.
The improvement survives restart without breaking protection, backup or required apps.
escalateWhen: Drive disconnects, read errors or physical damage appear.
A proposed optimization disables required functionality without evidence.

windows-repair.goal: Repair the component store and protected system files, then retest the feature that failed.
windows-repair.startHere: Check stable storage, saved work and a recovery copy. The online repair commands below apply to the running Windows installation, not an unverified WinRE drive.

tools.why: Repair the running Windows component store.
Verify protected files after component-store repair.
Reinstall the current Windows version while keeping apps, files and settings, when available.
Finding the failure rule and related log evidence before retrying an unsuccessful Windows upgrade.
Comparing a saved configuration with the changed version or checking a copied folder before accepting a repair or migration.

resources.label: Microsoft DISM and SFC sequence
resources.description: Run the documented repair order and read the final result.

resources.label: Repair an image and choose a source
resources.description: Match the installed version and correct online/offline target.

resources.label: Recovery options
resources.description: Choose a supported next step if servicing cannot repair the installation.

resources.label: Repair reinstall through Windows Update
resources.description: Use the supported same-version repair; managed update policies can make it unavailable.

decisions.symptom: Windows runs but a component or system file is corrupt
decisions.action: Open Terminal or Command Prompt as administrator; run DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth and wait for the final result.
decisions.expected: The operation completes successfully or supplies a specific error for the next branch.

decisions.symptom: DISM completes successfully
decisions.action: Run sfc /scannow in that elevated online session and retain its final message.
decisions.expected: SFC reports no corruption, repaired corruption or an explicit unresolved result.

decisions.symptom: DISM cannot find repair files
decisions.action: Record the error and OS build; follow Microsoft’s matching-source instructions instead of obtaining DLLs from third-party sites.
decisions.expected: A compatible source is identified and the repair can complete.

decisions.symptom: Repair reports success but the symptom remains
decisions.action: Restart if required, repeat the original feature test and distinguish an application-only fault from recurring system corruption.
decisions.expected: The actual failure is resolved or has an evidenced next owner.

decisions.symptom: Windows starts but system/update corruption persists
decisions.action: With saved work, recovery access, stable power and internet, open Settings > System > Recovery > Fix problems using Windows Update > Reinstall now if available. If managed policy hides it, use the organization’s repair route.
decisions.expected: The same Windows version is repaired, apps/files/settings remain, and the original failed task or update succeeds after restart.

doneWhen: The final DISM/SFC results and relevant logs are retained privately.
The original failing feature works after the required restart.
escalateWhen: Corruption returns with I/O errors or other storage symptoms.
The installation is nonrepairable or the correct target/source is uncertain.

windows-update.goal: Install the intended update or identify the exact policy, compatibility or servicing blocker.
windows-update.startHere: Open Settings > Windows Update > Update history. Record the failing KB, error and restart state before retrying.

tools.why: Run the supported update diagnostic.
Investigate component-store damage when the error points there.
Check protected files after successful servicing repair.
Reinstall the current Windows version while keeping apps, files and settings, when available.
Finding the failure rule and related log evidence before retrying an unsuccessful Windows upgrade.

resources.label: Windows Update troubleshooter
resources.description: Run the diagnostic, restart when required and check updates again.

resources.label: Troubleshoot update failures
resources.description: Use the exact error and installation stage.

resources.label: Windows release health
resources.description: Check the affected Windows version for known issues or holds.

resources.label: Recovery and uninstall choices
resources.description: Use the appropriate rollback route if the update prevents startup.

resources.label: Repair reinstall through Windows Update
resources.description: Use the supported same-version repair; managed update policies can make it unavailable.

decisions.symptom: One update repeatedly fails
decisions.action: Record its KB/error, check free space and connection, then run the Windows Update troubleshooter in Windows Get Help.
decisions.expected: The diagnostic gives a finding or a reproducible update error.

decisions.symptom: A restart is pending
decisions.action: Save work and restart in the agreed window, then return to Windows Update and Update history.
decisions.expected: The update completes or the same failing KB is identified after restart.

decisions.symptom: The device is managed or a compatibility hold is present
decisions.action: Check the organization’s update owner and the applicable release-health notice; do not bypass the hold or policy.
decisions.expected: The approved next update or remediation is recorded.

decisions.symptom: The update prevents Windows from starting
decisions.action: With recovery access ready, use WinRE > Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Uninstall Updates when the affected update is the established cause.
decisions.expected: The device returns to a bootable state for a scoped recovery plan.

decisions.symptom: Windows starts but system/update corruption persists
decisions.action: With saved work, recovery access, stable power and internet, open Settings > System > Recovery > Fix problems using Windows Update > Reinstall now if available. If managed policy hides it, use the organization’s repair route.
decisions.expected: The same Windows version is repaired, apps/files/settings remain, and the original failed task or update succeeds after restart.

doneWhen: Update history shows the intended result and no required restart remains.
The original application and a normal reboot succeed.
escalateWhen: The next step would bypass a managed policy or documented safeguard without an approved plan.
Boot or storage failure changes the job into recovery.

boot-recovery.goal: Restore a normal boot while preserving required data and encryption recovery.
boot-recovery.startHere: Record the exact startup screen. Check whether firmware sees the disk and whether BitLocker recovery material is available before repair.

tools.why: Open built-in startup and recovery tools.
Create trusted repair media on a working PC.
Preserve an unstable disk before boot-repair writes.
Check for a matching cloud remedy on eligible, configured devices with a widespread startup failure.

resources.label: Enter Windows Recovery Environment
resources.description: Use supported recovery media or the available advanced-startup path.

resources.label: Find the matching BitLocker recovery key
resources.description: Match the on-screen key ID with the approved personal or organization recovery record.

resources.label: Diagnose the failed boot stage
resources.description: Separate firmware, boot manager, loader and OS failures.

resources.label: Choose a recovery operation
resources.description: Check the data and application effects before reset or reinstall.

resources.label: Quick machine recovery — conditional
resources.description: Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.4700 or later; verify policy, network access and a matching remedy. Enterprise defaults can be off.

decisions.symptom: Firmware does not list the intended disk
decisions.action: Check the correct storage device and connection using the hardware procedure; stop if the disk is unstable.
decisions.expected: The disk is detected consistently or the job is routed to hardware/data recovery.

decisions.symptom: BitLocker asks for a recovery key
decisions.action: Match the displayed key ID to the approved recovery record; keep the key out of the public ticket or wiki.
decisions.expected: The correct encrypted volume unlocks without a reset or format.

decisions.symptom: The disk is stable but Windows cannot start
decisions.action: Open WinRE > Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Repair for the identified installation.
decisions.expected: Startup Repair reports its result and a normal boot can be tested.

decisions.symptom: A broad known startup failure may have a cloud remedy
decisions.action: Check supported Quick machine recovery availability, network access and organization policy in the recovery interface.
decisions.expected: A remedy is offered and tested, or ordinary recovery continues without assuming a cloud fix exists.

decisions.symptom: A recent update or driver change is the established trigger
decisions.action: Use the applicable uninstall or restore choice in WinRE after confirming recovery access and data protection.
decisions.expected: Windows boots without losing the required files and the triggering change is documented.

doneWhen: The device boots normally twice and the user can open priority files.
The intended boot disk and encryption recovery remain available.
escalateWhen: The disk fails, disconnects or contains the only unprotected data copy.
Recovery keys or the identity of the target installation are uncertain.

failing-drive.goal: Preserve the source, recover from a copy and prove which priority files are usable.
failing-drive.startHere: Stop writing to the source. Clicking, impact damage or irreplaceable data warrants a recovery-specialist decision before more power-on time.

tools.why: Boot a ready recovery environment containing GNU ddrescue.
Optional quick health read on a stable device only if it will not delay image-first recovery; stop if instability appears.
Recover file contents from healthy media or an image.
Inspect partitions on a working copy when that branch is justified.

resources.label: GNU ddrescue imaging manual
resources.description: Use verified devices and a persistent mapfile before file-system repair.

resources.label: SystemRescue included recovery tools
resources.description: Confirm the imaging and identification tools in the boot environment.

resources.label: PhotoRec recovery steps
resources.description: Write recovered output to another disk and inspect actual files.

resources.label: TestDisk partition analysis
resources.description: Distinguish inspection from partition-table writes.

decisions.symptom: The drive clicks, was dropped or repeatedly disconnects
decisions.action: Stop repeated boots and scans; record symptoms and have the owner choose specialist recovery.
decisions.expected: The remaining recoverability is not consumed by routine repair attempts.

decisions.symptom: A damaged drive remains readable enough to image
decisions.action: Boot SystemRescue, identify source and destination by model/serial/size and follow GNU ddrescue with a mapfile on persistent healthy storage.
decisions.expected: An image and resumable mapfile preserve readable ranges and identify unreadable gaps.

decisions.symptom: Files were deleted from healthy media
decisions.action: Check backups first; otherwise run PhotoRec against the healthy source or image and save to a separate disk.
decisions.expected: Recovered files open successfully; lost names or folder structure are recorded.

decisions.symptom: The image is encrypted or recovery reports missing ranges
decisions.action: Obtain the correct recovery material and assess the client’s priority files on a working copy.
decisions.expected: Usable files and unrecoverable areas are explicitly distinguished.

doneWhen: Source and destination identities are recorded; when imaging was required, the image and mapfile identities are recorded.
Priority recovered files open in their actual applications.
Any unreadable ranges and missing files are documented before acceptance.
escalateWhen: There is physical damage or an unstable connection that prevents controlled imaging.
A proposed repair would write to the only source or overwrite an unverified destination.
Do not benchmark a suspected failing drive with CrystalDiskMark; preserve recoverability instead.

disk-migration.goal: Move a healthy system or approved files to the correct destination with a usable rollback copy.
disk-migration.startHere: Identify every disk by model, serial and capacity. Confirm the source is healthy, backed up and the chosen destination may be overwritten.

tools.why: Graphical image or clone workflow for healthy storage.
Copy approved file trees with an inspectable log.
Inventory and reapply approved application packages.
Check SMART warnings, temperature and available health data before any performance test.
Optional quick storage performance baseline on healthy media only; choose the intended drive and record comparable settings.
Synchronize an explicitly chosen healthy-data folder between approved machines; keep an independent backup.
Comparing a saved configuration with the changed version or checking a copied folder before accepting a repair or migration.

resources.label: Rescuezilla migration limitations
resources.description: Plan smaller-disk restores and preserve an unmodified backup.

resources.label: Robocopy reference
resources.description: Review source, destination and copy flags before execution.

resources.label: WinGet export
resources.description: Export supported application identities for later review.

resources.label: WinGet import
resources.description: Review and install approved packages; user data is separate.

decisions.symptom: The source shows read errors or instability
decisions.action: Change route to image-first recovery rather than treating the operation as routine migration.
decisions.expected: The source is preserved before intensive copy or resize work.

decisions.symptom: The destination is smaller than the source layout
decisions.action: Check the tool’s supported geometry and create a rollback image before any separately planned resize.
decisions.expected: The target layout fits by evidence, not merely by free-space assumptions.

decisions.symptom: A complete healthy drive must be moved
decisions.action: Boot Rescuezilla, verify source/destination identities, then confirm the deliberate clone or restore operation.
decisions.expected: The operation completes and the destination can be booted by itself.

decisions.symptom: Only approved files need moving
decisions.action: Choose exact source and destination folders, review Robocopy flags and retain its result log; do not use a mirror/delete option by default.
decisions.expected: Expected files, timestamps and access are verified at the new location.

decisions.symptom: The copied system is ready for release
decisions.action: Boot with the old disk disconnected and test sign-in, applications, encryption recovery and backup.
decisions.expected: The new system works independently and the old disk remains the agreed rollback copy.

decisions.symptom: Storage is healthy but unusually slow, or a replacement drive needs a baseline
decisions.action: Check CrystalDiskInfo first. If storage is stable and backed up, use CrystalDiskMark with a bounded test file on the intended drive; compare the same profile, test size, count, connection and software version. Stop on disconnects or I/O errors.
decisions.expected: A reproducible read/write baseline for that drive, separate from SMART health; abnormal results lead to cable, port, controller or workload investigation, not a health diagnosis.

doneWhen: The destination boots independently or the copied file set passes application checks.
Required access, recovery material and backup work on the destination.
escalateWhen: Source/destination identity or erase permission is ambiguous.
Storage failure or incompatible target geometry makes the planned migration unsafe.

backup-restore.goal: Restore the required recovery point to a safe destination and verify real files or a complete system.
backup-restore.startHere: Identify the existing backup product, repository, recovery point and credentials. Use the matching restore tool rather than converting formats during an incident.

tools.why: Restore an existing supported Windows-agent backup.
Inspect and restore an existing restic repository.
Restore files from an existing Kopia snapshot.

resources.description: Check repository integrity before declaring a backup usable.

resources.label: restic restore procedure
resources.description: Choose the snapshot and a separate restore destination.

resources.label: Start Veeam file-level restore
resources.description: Launch the restore wizard and choose the existing backup and recovery point.

resources.label: Kopia snapshot restoration
resources.description: Use the GUI snapshot browser or documented CLI restore to a separate folder.

resources.label: Veeam recovery media and bare-metal restore
resources.description: Use compatible recovery media for an existing image backup; verify the target before overwrite.

decisions.symptom: A file or folder must be restored
decisions.action: Select the correct device and snapshot date in the matching backup tool and restore to a separate location.
decisions.expected: The expected version exists without overwriting the current working copy.

decisions.symptom: The existing backup is a Veeam Agent backup
decisions.action: Open File Level Restore from the Veeam Start-menu entry, select the backup and restore point, then copy the required files to a separate destination in the backup browser.
decisions.expected: The restored version opens correctly before any working file is replaced.

decisions.symptom: The existing backup is a Kopia snapshot
decisions.action: Connect KopiaUI to the existing repository, open Snapshots, select the source Path and dated snapshot, then restore the required item to a separate folder.
decisions.expected: The selected files exist in the restore folder and open with the expected contents.

decisions.symptom: A restic backup reports success but has not been tested
decisions.action: Inspect its snapshots, run the documented repository check and restore representative files to a separate target.
decisions.expected: The recovery point and usable contents are demonstrated rather than inferred from a green job.

decisions.symptom: A whole computer must be recovered
decisions.action: Use that backup product’s compatible recovery media and check storage/network drivers before selecting the erase target.
decisions.expected: The restored system boots and its critical application opens the expected data.

decisions.symptom: A password, repository or required snapshot is missing
decisions.action: Record the exact missing dependency and contact its owner before modifying the repository.
decisions.expected: The recovery gap has an owner and the remaining copies stay intact.

doneWhen: The requested recovery date and a real file/application test are recorded.
Permissions and ownership allow the intended user to work.
Measured restore time and missing data are documented.
escalateWhen: The only backup would be overwritten or exposed to an active compromise.
Required credentials or a valid recovery point cannot be established.

network-dns.goal: Find the failed link, address, name-resolution or service connection and retest the real task.
network-dns.startHere: Compare another device on the same network. Establish whether the fault affects this PC, one service, the VPN or the whole office.

tools.why: Run supported local connection diagnostics.
Read IP, DNS and connection results on the affected PC.
Capture only a scoped unresolved protocol failure.
Separating DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP failures when a web service or application endpoint is unreachable.
Comparing a reproducible path problem from a Linux or macOS bench, or Windows through WSL.

resources.label: Windows network troubleshooting
resources.description: Work through local connection checks before a network reset.

resources.label: Get-NetIPConfiguration
resources.description: Read the active adapter, address, gateway and DNS servers.

resources.label: Resolve-DnsName
resources.description: Test the actual failing service name.

resources.label: Test-NetConnection
resources.description: Test the service’s documented TCP port.

decisions.symptom: Only this PC is disconnected
decisions.action: Check cable/Wi-Fi state and run the Network and Internet diagnostic in Windows Get Help.
decisions.expected: The active link is identified and the diagnostic has a specific result.

decisions.symptom: The PC has no usable gateway or a self-assigned IPv4 address
decisions.action: Run Get-NetIPConfiguration; compare the active adapter with the approved DHCP/network configuration.
decisions.expected: The PC receives the intended address, gateway and DNS rather than an invented static setting.

decisions.symptom: IP connectivity works but a hostname fails
decisions.action: Run Resolve-DnsName for that service name and compare the configured DNS server with a working client.
decisions.expected: The correct answer resolves or the faulty DNS dependency is identified.

decisions.symptom: The name resolves but the application cannot connect
decisions.action: Run Test-NetConnection for the target’s documented TCP port and compare a working path; a successful TCP test still needs the app test.
decisions.expected: The evidence distinguishes blocked transport from an application or authentication failure.

decisions.symptom: Many devices or only VPN users fail
decisions.action: Use the shared-network or managed-VPN owner and preserve adapter, route and DNS settings before disruptive changes.
decisions.expected: The shared dependency has a scoped repair plan and owner.

doneWhen: The original site, share or application works by its normal hostname.
Required VPN and business connectivity still work after the change.
escalateWhen: The fault is a shared outage or managed-policy issue outside local authority.
The next action would reset production networking without a recovery path.

outage-recovery.goal: Restore the actual business service in dependency order and verify it from a user device.
outage-recovery.startHere: Confirm safe power and identify the affected service. Assign one recovery owner before restarting shared systems.

tools.why: Inspect recovered Windows services and connection state.
Check for a matching cloud remedy on eligible, configured devices with a widespread startup failure.
Separating DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP failures when a web service or application endpoint is unreachable.
Comparing a reproducible path problem from a Linux or macOS bench, or Windows through WSL.

resources.label: Interpret unexpected-restart evidence
resources.description: Event 41 alone does not identify the shutdown cause.

resources.label: Quick machine recovery — conditional
resources.description: Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.4700 or later; verify policy, network access and a matching remedy. Enterprise defaults can be off.

resources.label: Verify a backup restore
resources.description: Prove the recovery point and actual restored application.

resources.label: Record owners and outstanding faults
resources.description: Keep the service timeline and next actions in the private record.

decisions.symptom: Power or hardware is visibly unsafe
decisions.action: Stop repeated power cycling and involve the qualified power or hardware owner.
decisions.expected: The equipment can be energized safely or remains isolated for repair.

decisions.symptom: Network is back but storage or hosts are not ready
decisions.action: Inspect the relevant console and storage status before starting dependent workloads; do not initialize or format missing volumes.
decisions.expected: The required storage and host resources are stable before application recovery.

decisions.symptom: Identity or DNS is unavailable
decisions.action: Restore the approved identity/network dependencies in the site runbook, then test name resolution and sign-in from a client.
decisions.expected: The user can authenticate and reach the required service names.

decisions.symptom: Services show running but users still cannot work
decisions.action: Test the actual application and its data/share/database dependency from a normal user session.
decisions.expected: A real transaction or equivalent business task succeeds.

decisions.symptom: Many supported Windows 11 endpoints fail at startup
decisions.action: Check the common change and whether Quick machine recovery is enabled and applicable; use the normal recovery plan if no remedy is available.
decisions.expected: A verified remedy or a controlled rollback is chosen without assuming cloud recovery will succeed.

doneWhen: Critical user workflows succeed from the affected network.
Backup operation and remaining infrastructure alarms have been checked.
The timeline, cause evidence and follow-up owner are recorded.
escalateWhen: Storage/RAID damage, unsafe power or active compromise changes the recovery route.
The required restore would overwrite the only recovery copy.

remote-support.goal: Connect through the appropriate approved channel, complete the task and close temporary access.
remote-support.startHere: Confirm the user and helper through the existing support channel. Decide whether the session is attended or requires an approved managed agent.

tools.why: One-time attended Windows help.
Approved cross-platform or self-hosted support.
Existing managed-device access and service oversight.
Connecting a Linux technician workstation to an already configured remote desktop or server.

decisions.symptom: A Windows user is present and can approve a session
decisions.action: Open Microsoft Quick Assist on both PCs, exchange the temporary code and have the user approve sharing and any separate control request.
decisions.expected: The correct screen is visible and the user understands the control state.

decisions.symptom: The task requires unattended access or durable audit records
decisions.action: Use the approved managed tool and existing device identity; verify the technician’s role before connecting.
decisions.expected: The session is tied to the intended asset and required audit record.

decisions.symptom: Elevation or a secure-desktop prompt blocks work
decisions.action: Have the authorized local user respond or use the approved managed elevation workflow; do not ask for credentials in chat.
decisions.expected: The required action is approved without disclosing credentials or bypassing consent.

decisions.symptom: The repair appears complete
decisions.action: Repeat the original task with the user, end the session and remove any case-only access setting.
decisions.expected: The user confirms the outcome and temporary control has ended.

doneWhen: The original task works in the user’s session.
The session is closed and authorized persistent access is documented.
escalateWhen: The user/helper identity or device target cannot be verified.
Requested access exceeds the approved session or exposes an active compromise.

ad-trust.goal: Repair a confirmed domain-member secure-channel fault and prove normal domain access.
ad-trust.startHere: Use the affected member PC. Check its domain DNS, time and domain-controller reachability before considering a trust repair.

tools.why: Use existing Windows PowerShell 5.1 on the member PC.
Establishing recoverable, per-device administrator access during managed workstation setup and support planning.

resources.label: Test-ComputerSecureChannel
resources.description: Read-only test first; repair only a confirmed member-computer fault.

resources.label: Microsoft trust-relationship troubleshooting
resources.description: Check connectivity, identity and the cause before rejoining.

resources.label: Read the member PC network configuration
resources.description: Confirm the intended domain DNS path.

decisions.symptom: Domain names or controllers cannot be reached
decisions.action: Correct the approved network/VPN, DNS or time issue before touching the computer account.
decisions.expected: The member can resolve and reach its expected domain services.

decisions.symptom: Connectivity is correct but the trust error remains
decisions.action: Open Windows PowerShell 5.1 as administrator on the member PC and run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Verbose.
decisions.expected: True confirms that this channel works; False supplies evidence for the scoped repair branch.

decisions.symptom: A member secure-channel fault is confirmed
decisions.action: With approved repair rights and local recovery access, run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair -Credential (Get-Credential) -Verbose in that elevated member-PC session; enter delegated credentials only in the prompt.
decisions.expected: The diagnostic returns True after repair.

decisions.symptom: The device is a domain controller or many devices fail
decisions.action: Use the domain-administration incident route instead of this member-only cmdlet.
decisions.expected: The correct infrastructure owner investigates the wider fault.

doneWhen: The member secure-channel test succeeds.
A normal domain sign-in and required shared resource work.
escalateWhen: The target is a domain controller or the issue affects the wider domain.
Repair authority, local recovery access or the device identity is uncertain.

outlook-email.goal: Separate a mail-service failure from a local client problem and prove send, receive and the affected shared feature.
outlook-email.startHere: Test the same account in webmail and identify classic Outlook versus new Outlook before changing a local profile.

tools.why: Choose a diagnostic for classic Outlook only.
Separating DNS, TCP, TLS and HTTP failures when a web service or application endpoint is unreachable.

resources.label: Classic Outlook diagnostics
resources.description: Choose startup, authentication or connectivity; not for new Outlook.

resources.label: New and classic Outlook repair branches
resources.description: Use the tab matching the installed client.

resources.label: New Outlook architecture and differences
resources.description: Check the client’s supported behavior before applying a classic-only fix.

decisions.symptom: Webmail also fails or several users are affected
decisions.action: Capture the sign-in/send error and compare another affected account; involve the mail or identity service owner.
decisions.expected: The fault is identified as service, account or policy scope rather than a local profile guess.

decisions.symptom: Classic Outlook will not start or repeatedly asks for credentials
decisions.action: Open the matching classic Outlook diagnostic in Windows Get Help on the affected PC.
decisions.expected: The test identifies a startup, authentication or connectivity finding.

decisions.symptom: Only classic Outlook fails and an add-in is suspected
decisions.action: Press Win+R, run outlook.exe /safe and compare the same task; record enabled add-ins before changing one.
decisions.expected: The safe-mode comparison establishes whether the add-in branch is relevant.

decisions.symptom: New Outlook is the affected client
decisions.action: Preserve unsent work where possible; in Task Manager select Microsoft Outlook > End task, then reopen new Outlook and repeat the failing task. If it still fails, follow Microsoft’s new-client reinstall branch after protecting local-only mail.
decisions.expected: The supported new-client path restores the failing task or identifies its service dependency.

decisions.symptom: A profile rebuild or data-file repair is proposed
decisions.action: Identify PST/local-only mail and preserve it before changing the profile or file.
decisions.expected: No unique mail is lost while the repaired client is tested.

doneWhen: Send and receive succeed for the affected account.
The affected calendar, shared mailbox or attachment workflow works.
Local-only data is preserved and the actual client/version is recorded.
escalateWhen: Local-only mail lacks a protected copy.
The fault involves tenant policy, identity compromise or a wider service outage.

printer-repair.goal: Print the original document with the intended device and options; verify scanning separately for multifunction devices.
printer-repair.startHere: Read the make/model and IP from the printer’s own network/configuration report. On the PC open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners and select the intended queue.

tools.why: Run the supported printer diagnostic.
Find the printer’s current address within an approved local subnet.
Read the exact installed queue, driver and port.
Test scanner, feeder and multipage PDF output.
Identifying the actual USB port, hub, device and negotiated connection when a printer, scanner or peripheral disconnects or runs slowly.
Testing the same known-good PDF through an independent renderer to separate an application-specific print fault from the queue or printer.

decisions.symptom: The printer cannot print its own internal page
decisions.action: Resolve paper, consumables, displayed errors and hardware state before changing the PC.
decisions.expected: The device produces its own clean test/configuration page.

decisions.symptom: The printer IP is unknown
decisions.action: Print the printer’s network report or check its approved DHCP record. If still needed, scan only the authorized local subnet with Advanced IP Scanner and match the device using its physical model and MAC address.
decisions.expected: The address is tied to the intended printer, not merely an open port.

decisions.symptom: The queue is offline or targets an old address
decisions.action: Run Get-Printer | Format-Table Name,PortName,DriverName and Get-PrinterPort in Windows PowerShell 5.1; compare the target with the network report.
decisions.expected: The selected queue uses the correct live device and connection.

decisions.symptom: A driver reinstall or vendor package is being considered
decisions.action: Check Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners for Windows protected print mode and managed policy; use supported IPP/Mopria and a vendor Print Support App when WPP applies.
decisions.expected: The chosen print path is compatible with the active security mode; a legacy package is not forced onto WPP.

decisions.symptom: A conventional driver is actually required
decisions.action: Use Windows Update or the exact manufacturer link above; match model, Windows version and x64/ARM architecture before installation.
decisions.expected: The supported driver installs for this device and retains required trays, duplex and color options.

decisions.symptom: One job or application fails
decisions.action: Cancel only the affected stuck job when appropriate, test a Windows test page and print from another app before changing a shared queue.
decisions.expected: The failing job/application is distinguished from a device-wide or queue-wide fault.

decisions.symptom: Printing works but scanning fails
decisions.action: In NAPS2 choose New Profile > Choose device. Select a supported WIA/TWAIN device, or eSCL for a compatible network scanner; scan a page and save/open the PDF. Test the feeder and duplex if required.
decisions.expected: The saved PDF contains every intended page in the correct order; scanning works independently of the print queue.

doneWhen: The original document prints with correct page size, tray, duplex and color.
Another user can still print through any shared queue.
Required scan/ADF output opens correctly and the model, IP, port and driver are recorded.
escalateWhen: Changing a shared spooler/driver would interrupt other users without coordination.
Protected-print policy, ARM compatibility or unsupported hardware requires the managed print owner.

hardware-bsod.goal: Use repeatable crash evidence to identify the failing driver, component or operating condition.
hardware-bsod.startHere: Record the stop code, crash time and recent changes. Check storage health and safe temperatures before load testing.

tools.why: Read the recorded crash dump and stack.
Test memory outside the running OS when evidence points there.
Observe sensor behavior without claiming a sensor alone proves the cause.
Check storage warnings before further stress.
Optional quick storage performance baseline on healthy media only; choose the intended drive and record comparable settings.
Identifying the actual USB port, hub, device and negotiated connection when a printer, scanner or peripheral disconnects or runs slowly.
Collecting battery and sleep evidence before changing hardware or power policy.
Measure a reproducible storage-performance problem on healthy media with a bounded test file.

resources.description: Correlate stop codes, changes and relevant hardware tests.

resources.description: Open the dump and inspect analysis in the correct context.

resources.description: Event 41 is a symptom record, not proof of a failed PSU.

resources.label: Memtest86+ boot and error guidance
resources.description: Match firmware support and record the tested configuration.

decisions.symptom: A crash dump is available
decisions.action: Open it in WinDbg and run !analyze -v; compare the stop code and stack with other failures and the change timeline.
decisions.expected: Repeated evidence identifies a driver/component branch; one named module is not treated as proof by itself.

decisions.symptom: Crashes began after a specific driver or hardware change
decisions.action: Use the exact vendor-supported rollback or correction for that identified change and repeat the failing workload.
decisions.expected: The same reproduction no longer crashes, or the hypothesis is rejected.

decisions.symptom: Evidence points to RAM instability
decisions.action: Record firmware/overclock settings, boot Memtest86+ and isolate modules or slots using the hardware procedure.
decisions.expected: Errors are reproduced and narrowed to a configuration, or the test result is recorded without excluding other causes.

decisions.symptom: The system overheats, loses power or storage disappears
decisions.action: Stop stress testing and inspect the indicated cooling, power or storage path with the appropriate service guidance.
decisions.expected: The physical fault is addressed before further workload testing.

decisions.symptom: Storage is healthy but unusually slow, or a replacement drive needs a baseline
decisions.action: Check CrystalDiskInfo first. If storage is stable and backed up, use CrystalDiskMark with a bounded test file on the intended drive; compare the same profile, test size, count, connection and software version. Stop on disconnects or I/O errors.
decisions.expected: A reproducible read/write baseline for that drive, separate from SMART health; abnormal results lead to cable, port, controller or workload investigation, not a health diagnosis.

doneWhen: The same workload runs without a new crash after the evidenced correction.
Crash/test results, firmware settings and any component change are recorded.
escalateWhen: There is unsafe temperature, electrical damage or unstable storage.
The fault requires disassembly or specialist testing beyond the available service capability.

new-pc.goal: Deliver a supported workstation whose identity, apps, files, recovery and backup work for its owner.
new-pc.startHere: Confirm the owner, organization enrollment method, required apps and migrated data. Check Settings > System > About for the actual Windows version and architecture.

tools.why: Identify and install approved application packages.
Check SMART warnings, temperature and available health data before any performance test.
Optional quick storage performance baseline on healthy media only; choose the intended drive and record comparable settings.
Use the exact device vendor’s supported drivers and firmware.
Move only the agreed files with a reviewed copy plan.
Evaluate an approved package in a disposable desktop with network and shared-folder exposure explicitly configured.

Starting an approved installer or rescue environment through network boot or remote virtual media when local media delivery is inconvenient.
Establishing recoverable, per-device administrator access during managed workstation setup and support planning.

resources.description: Reapply an approved inventory; licenses and user data remain separate.

resources.description: Use Windows Update and the correct device/manufacturer route.

decisions.symptom: The device is new or has a fresh installation
decisions.action: Complete the approved enrollment and Windows/OEM updates, then check Device Manager for unresolved devices.
decisions.expected: The intended identity and basic hardware work without unexplained device faults.

decisions.symptom: Approved applications must be installed
decisions.action: Use WinGet search/show to confirm package identity and review installation or the approved import list.
decisions.expected: Each required app launches with the correct license and user context.

decisions.symptom: Data comes from the previous device
decisions.action: Copy the agreed data using the migration plan and test representative files in their real applications.
decisions.expected: The user can access the expected files without relying on the old device.

decisions.symptom: Setup is nearly complete
decisions.action: Verify encryption recovery storage, a backup restore, printing and the user’s daily workflow before handoff.
decisions.expected: The workstation is usable and recoverable, with acceptance evidence recorded.

decisions.symptom: Storage is healthy but unusually slow, or a replacement drive needs a baseline
decisions.action: Check CrystalDiskInfo first. If storage is stable and backed up, use CrystalDiskMark with a bounded test file on the intended drive; compare the same profile, test size, count, connection and software version. Stop on disconnects or I/O errors.
decisions.expected: A reproducible read/write baseline for that drive, separate from SMART health; abnormal results lead to cable, port, controller or workload investigation, not a health diagnosis.

doneWhen: The owner can sign in and complete the agreed daily tasks.
Recovery material and a tested backup are accessible through the approved private process.
escalateWhen: Enrollment, licensing or recovery ownership is unclear.
Migration would endanger the only copy of user data.

client-handoff.goal: Close the case with user-visible proof, clean access and a clear next owner.
client-handoff.startHere: Repeat the original requested task with the user before declaring the repair complete.

tools.why: Comparing a saved configuration with the changed version or checking a copied folder before accepting a repair or migration.

resources.label: Technician handoff template
resources.description: Record cause, changes, tests, limits and ownership.

resources.label: Service acceptance evidence
resources.description: Record observations rather than a generic “fixed” status.

resources.label: Public knowledge and private case material
resources.description: Keep credentials, recovery keys and customer evidence in the private record.

decisions.symptom: The repair looks successful
decisions.action: Have the user perform the original task and record its actual result, including required peripherals or shared access.
decisions.expected: The acceptance evidence matches the requested outcome.

decisions.symptom: Temporary remote access or one-case tools remain
decisions.action: End temporary sessions, remove case-only access settings and confirm approved persistent management still works.
decisions.expected: The device has no unplanned temporary access or monitoring.

decisions.symptom: Some work is deferred or uncertain
decisions.action: Record the exact remaining symptom, next action, owner and follow-up time.
decisions.expected: Another technician can continue without repeating completed diagnostics.

decisions.symptom: Recovery information must be handed over
decisions.action: Store the approved private reference and confirm the authorized owner can retrieve it; do not paste the secret into the public wiki.
decisions.expected: The recovery path is usable without exposing credentials.

doneWhen: The user accepts the demonstrated result or explicitly recorded limitation.
Changes, recovery references and follow-up ownership are complete.
escalateWhen: The original task still fails or acceptance cannot be demonstrated.
Temporary access or required recovery ownership remains unresolved.

boot-usb.goal: Prepare verified rescue or installation media that boots and sees the required hardware.
boot-usb.startHere: Identify the USB by model, capacity and contents; copy off anything that must be kept before a write operation.

tools.why: Write one selected official ISO to the intended USB.
Maintain a verified multiboot collection.
Obtain supported Windows repair/install media.
Provide an independent imaging and recovery environment.
Starting an approved installer or rescue environment through network boot or remote virtual media when local media delivery is inconvenient.

resources.label: Rufus operation and firmware choices
resources.description: Confirm image, target USB and the intended boot mode.

resources.label: Ventoy install versus update
resources.description: Distinguish a destructive install from updating existing media.

resources.label: Verify a selected file hash
resources.description: Compare the exact downloaded image with its publisher’s checksum.

resources.label: Ventoy Secure Boot instructions
resources.description: Review image/firmware support and recovery before changing keys or settings.

decisions.symptom: Only one rescue or installation image is needed
decisions.action: Use the official ISO and Rufus; confirm the selected USB can be erased and choose firmware-compatible options.
decisions.expected: The intended image is written to the correct device.

decisions.symptom: Several verified images must stay on one USB
decisions.action: Use the documented Ventoy install/update path and copy the checked images to its data partition.
decisions.expected: The expected images appear in the boot menu.

decisions.symptom: The publisher supplies a checksum
decisions.action: Run Get-FileHash for the exact downloaded file and compare it with the official value before writing.
decisions.expected: The calculated hash matches the trusted release record.

decisions.symptom: Writing finished but the client may have unusual hardware
decisions.action: Boot-test the intended firmware mode and verify keyboard, storage, network and the required recovery tool.
decisions.expected: The actual service path works on representative hardware rather than only completing an image write.

doneWhen: Image source, hash and release are recorded.
The USB boots and detects the hardware required for the planned job.
escalateWhen: The target USB or its erase permission is uncertain.
A firmware/security change lacks the necessary recovery material.

ai-triage.goal: Use AI to choose a justified diagnostic and produce a factual service note.
ai-triage.startHere: Prepare the exact error, timing and environment with customer identities, credentials, internal addresses and file contents removed.

tools.why: Compare hypotheses and explain sanitized evidence.
Review a scoped script or code change in an approved workspace.
Evaluate an approved package in a disposable desktop with network and shared-folder exposure explicitly configured.
Checking whether a revised diagnostic prompt handles a sanitized regression set correctly before relying on it in technician workflows.

resources.label: ChatGPT data controls
resources.description: Check the approved account/workspace controls before sharing evidence.

resources.label: Codex CLI documentation
resources.description: Use a defined workspace and review the proposed execution scope.

resources.label: NIST generative-AI profile
resources.description: Check generated claims, sources and proposed actions against evidence.

decisions.symptom: The failure has several plausible causes
decisions.action: Provide the sanitized reproduction and ask for ranked causes plus one small test that separates the leading possibilities.
decisions.expected: The output distinguishes observations from assumptions and predicts a test result.

decisions.symptom: The assistant proposes a command
decisions.action: Check the exact target, shell, privileges, writes and rollback against the official product documentation before execution.
decisions.expected: The technician understands and approves the scoped action.

decisions.symptom: A test contradicts the proposed cause
decisions.action: Return the exact sanitized result and require a revised hypothesis rather than repeating an unchanged failed action.
decisions.expected: The next diagnostic follows the new evidence.

decisions.symptom: The repair is ready to document
decisions.action: Draft the cause/change/test note from verified observations, then review it before saving.
decisions.expected: The handoff contains demonstrated facts and explicit remaining uncertainty.

doneWhen: The original task passes a real test independent of the AI answer.
Executed actions match the actual environment and no unnecessary private content was shared.
escalateWhen: The proposed action is destructive, unsupported or lacks a verified target.
The organization has not approved the intended data/account boundary.

preventive-maintenance.goal: Complete a useful health, update and recovery check without disrupting the user’s working setup.
preventive-maintenance.startHere: Agree the maintenance window and identify the user’s current problem. Verify a usable backup before changes.

Collecting battery and sleep evidence before changing hardware or power policy.
Establishing recoverable, per-device administrator access during managed workstation setup and support planning.

decisions.symptom: The device has recurring failures or storage warnings
decisions.action: Check Reliability Monitor and drive health; move actual faults to their repair or recovery guide before routine maintenance.
decisions.expected: The maintenance plan is based on observed faults rather than cleanup rituals.

decisions.symptom: Application updates are available
decisions.action: Run winget upgrade to list them, review compatibility and update only the approved packages in the maintenance window.
decisions.expected: The selected versions are installed and any planned restart is completed.

decisions.symptom: A full disk or missing local file is the concern
decisions.action: Use WinDirStat for capacity or Everything for a filename; confirm ownership and retention before deleting or moving anything.
decisions.expected: The relevant path is identified and any approved cleanup has a measured result.

decisions.symptom: Backup jobs report success
decisions.action: Restore a representative item to a separate location and open it with the intended application.
decisions.expected: The backup is demonstrably usable, with its recovery point recorded.

decisions.symptom: Changes are complete
decisions.action: Restart as planned and repeat the user’s main app, network, printing and backup checks.
decisions.expected: Normal work succeeds and all deferred issues have owners.

decisions.symptom: Storage is healthy but unusually slow, or a replacement drive needs a baseline
decisions.action: Check CrystalDiskInfo first. If storage is stable and backed up, use CrystalDiskMark with a bounded test file on the intended drive; compare the same profile, test size, count, connection and software version. Stop on disconnects or I/O errors.
decisions.expected: A reproducible read/write baseline for that drive, separate from SMART health; abnormal results lead to cable, port, controller or workload investigation, not a health diagnosis.

doneWhen: Protection, hardware health and backup restoration have been checked.
The normal workload works after maintenance and restart.
Each unresolved item has an explicit next action and owner.
escalateWhen: Storage failure or active compromise changes the service route.
An unplanned critical workload would be interrupted.
